text:
emma_support: Novus-Pay is seeing sustained throttling on their Dedicated pool dp-prod-7. Customer reports periodic 429s, high latency, and a spike in billing usage last night. They say this started after flipping on long-context for a subset of routes (~50k tokens).

raj_engineering: I can see the alerts — kv_cache_evictions spiked and p99 latency for token-gen jumped. Quick Prometheus dump I grabbed: 
```
kv_cache_evictions_total{tenant="novus-pay"} 8460
kv_cache_evictions_rate{tenant="novus-pay"} 142.3
kv_cache_mem_used_bytes{tenant="novus-pay"} 1.9e+10
kv_cache_frag_ratio{pool="dp-prod-7"} 0.62
serving_request_429_total{pool="dp-prod-7"} 230
serving_p99_latency_ms{pool="dp-prod-7"} 1420
```
Looks like eviction churn + fragmentation.

lucy_oncall: Reproduced locally against dp-prod-7 with a 50k token prefix stress test (small loop of 30 concurrent sessions). Observed repeated slab frees then realloct at high rate, and a cascade: more evictions => higher KV misses => more work per request => more memory pressure => autoscaler not stepping up fast enough. Getting 503s when the runtime hits internal OOM-protections and 429s at API layer.

autoscale-bot: Autoscaler event: pool=dp-prod-7 scale_decision=NOOP reason="cooldown" next_evaluation_in=120s; current_replicas=4 min_replicas=4 max_replicas=8 cooldown=300s

emma_support: Customer also reported spikes in auth errors during retries (they saw a flurry of 401s around the same time). Could be client-side token expiry interacting with retry-backoff causing amplified load.

raj_engineering: Two quick hypotheses: (1) long-context workloads increase KV entry sizes leading to fragmentation and slab blowouts, (2) noisy tenant caused constant eviction churn preventing reuse of cached prefixes so cost per request balloons. Both fit the metrics.

tim_support_lead: Suggested immediate mitigations we can propose to Novus-Pay: reduce their max_context to 32k, enable prefix-only caching for heavy routes, and set client-side retry jitter. Also ask infra to temporarily bump dp-prod-7 by +1 replica or raise max_replicas.

raj_engineering: Agreed. For infra: can we relax the scaler cooldown for this pool temporarily? Current cooldown prevents reactive scale-up during churn. Patch proposal: set cooldown=60s for dp-prod-7 and add an eviction-rate trigger that requests a scale when kv_cache_evictions_rate > 50 for > 30s.

lucy_oncall: Repro steps I used so others can validate: 
1) spawn 30 sessions hitting /v1/generate with context=50k tokens
2) call every 15s with random prefix to avoid cache hits
3) observe metrics via /metrics (prometheus) and check runtime logs: 
```
kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=runtime -c runtime --tail 200 | grep -E "evict|alloc|oom|kv_cache"
curl -s http://metrics.internal:9100/metrics | grep novus-pay
```
4) capture heap profiles from runtime admin endpoint /admin/heap (only on staging)

emma_support: Customer asked for timeline. Can we commit to a short-term fix + long-term? They'd prefer not to pause long-context entirely.

raj_engineering: Short-term: (a) bump replicas by +1, (b) temporary cooldown tweak, (c) recommend client changes to reduce concurrent long-contexts. Long-term: implement per-tenant cache budgeting and improve slab compaction to reduce frag ratio. I'll open a PR for the autoscaler trigger and a patch for slab compaction heuristics.

autoscale-bot: Action logged: ticket=INC-2026-83962 assigned=raj_engineering status=investigating

tim_support_lead: I'll message Novus-Pay with the mitigations and request logs (metrics snapshot + sample failing request ids). Also offering a temporary credit adjustment while we remediate.

lucy_oncall: After bumping 1 replica in staging and applying cooldown=60s we saw evictions drop ~78% and p99 latency fell to ~220ms in the test window. Will schedule a controlled change to production later today during low traffic.

emma_support: Thanks team. I'll update the thread with customer responses. For tracking: include ticket INC-2026-83962 in all follow-ups. :thumbsup:
